status: approved 2026-10-21 with the recommended defaults below; implemented as src/server/reference/region-decisions.ts (this file is not read by code)

pt-doc.title: Portuguese DOCs (top level): name and class agree
pt-doc.rationale: Wikidata labels them '(DOC)' and they carry the 'denominação de origem controlada' class. Name and class agree.

pt-doc-sub.title: Portuguese DOC sub-regions (child of a DOC)
pt-doc-sub.rationale: Named '(DOC)' and linked by Wikidata 'part of' to a parent DOC; 14 of 19 also carry the DOC class. Proposed: kind appellation, keeping the parent link, so the DOC→sub-region hierarchy survives. The alternative, kind 'subregion', would never fill anything: names with a designation are never offered as a subregion.

pt-ipr.title: Portuguese IPRs (Indicação de Proveniência Regulamentada)
pt-ipr.rationale: They carry the IPR class, a regulated designation of provenance. Proposed: appellation, keeping parent links to their DOC. Assumption: several IPRs have since been promoted to DOC or merged (e.g. Pico, Biscoitos, Graciosa, Lafões, Encostas da Nave, Varosa); the kind is appellation either way, but their current status needs the IVV register.

pt-vr.title: Portuguese Vinhos Regionais (VR)
pt-vr.rationale: They carry the 'Vinhos regionais' class. A VR is a broad regional indication (PGI level) and the closest thing in this catalog to a wine region, so they keep kind region. Assumption: a VR is broader than the DOCs inside it, so a VR must never be a DOC's child.

douro-port.title: Douro, Port and the RDD (parent loop)
douro-port.rationale: RDD and 'Port Wine' are each other's parent, which is a loop. RDD is the demarcated region that contains DOC Douro and DOC Porto. Proposed: RDD stays a region with no parent; Douro (DOC) and Port Wine become appellations under RDD; Alto Douro Wine Region (the UNESCO landscape) stays a separate region, not merged.

madeira.title: Madeira wine (DOC)
madeira.rationale: It carries the DOC class and is labelled '(DOC)', but the item is about the wine ('Madeira wine'). Proposed: appellation, and keep it (it is the only Madeira DOC record).

arrabida-dup.title: Duplicate 'Arrábida (IPR)': Q2879982
arrabida-dup.rationale: Two records share the label 'Arrábida (IPR)'. Q16010776 has the IPR class and sits under Palmela (DOC): the real Arrábida. Q2879982 has the DOC class, no parent, and its only alias is 'Bairrada (DOC)', so it is probably Bairrada DOC with a wrong English label. That can't be confirmed from the snapshot.

fr-aoc-name.title: French AOCs named 'X AOC'
fr-aoc-name.rationale: The Wikidata label itself ends in 'AOC'. Only Côtes-du-Rhône Villages AOC also carries the AOC class (high); the rest rest on the label alone (medium).

fr-aoc-alias.title: French AOCs with '(AOC)' only in an alias
fr-aoc-alias.rationale: Their aliases are '<name> (AOC)', and they carry no class besides wine-producing region. Assumption: these names are AOCs (true for all 14, from domain knowledge). Chenas and Côteaux du Giennois are also wrongly typed 'winery' in Wikidata; see their rows.

fr-other.title: Other French candidates (unflagged)
fr-other.rationale: Decided one by one: Beaujolais cru, Rhône village wine, vineyard area, wine region, hill range.

es-do-name.title: Spanish DOs named with the designation
es-do-name.rationale: The label carries DO, DOP or PDO. Tierra del Vino de Zamora DO also carries the 'appellation' class.

es-do-dual.title: Spanish DOs whose name is also the everyday region name
es-do-dual.rationale: Their aliases are DO or DOCa forms, but the bare name (Rioja, Ribera del Duero…) is also used as a region. Abona carries the 'appellation' class (evidence); the others are base-only. Proposed: appellation. Since PR #17, a label's appellation text never makes them the region anyway.

es-orotava.title: Valle de la Orotava (DO) vs Orotava Valley (valley)
es-orotava.rationale: Two records, one name. Q2509282 is the DO (aliases 'Denominación de Origen…', '(vino)'). Q1290583 is the valley (classes valley, landscape, comarca) and carries 'Valle de la Orotava' as an alias. Today both are regions with equal score, so a lookup of 'Valle de la Orotava' is marked ambiguous and fills nothing. Proposed: Q2509282 → appellation, Q1290583 stays region. Lookup then prefers the appellation and the ambiguity goes away.

es-pgi.title: Spanish PGIs (Vino de la Tierra)
es-pgi.rationale: Labelled 'PGI', with 'Vino de la Tierra' aliases. A PGI is a protected indication, not a designation of origin. The schema has only region/subregion/appellation; 'appellation' is the slot a label puts it in. Ribera del Queiles carries the 'designation of origin' class, which contradicts its label (assumption: the label is right; the register decides).

es-other.title: Sherry Triangle
es-other.rationale: Class 'region'; it's the geographic area (Marco de Jerez), not DO Jerez itself. Stays a region.

it-dup.title: Italian DOC duplicates and the items typed 'wine'
it-dup.rationale: Bivongi DOC, Friuli Annia DOC and Colli Romagna Centrale DOC are typed 'wine'. Bivongi and Friuli Annia also have a same-named region record (Q140131443 Bivongi, Q140131124 Friuli Annia). Colli Piacentini (typed 'hill group', alias 'Colli piacentini (DOC)') has a twin, Q140131139. Proposed: the DOC-labelled record becomes the appellation; whether to drop or keep the plain twins (Q14013xxxx, base class only) is your decision. Alto Adige is typed 'wine', and its aliases wrongly include 'Trentino'.

it-region.title: Italian areas typed 'region' (dual DOC/area names)
it-region.rationale: Wikidata types them as a region, hill chain, cultural landscape and so on. The same names are also DOC(G)s (Chianti, Roero, Valpolicella, Franciacorta…), but nothing in the evidence says the record is the designation. They stay regions; PR #17 already stops the appellation text making them the region. Franciacorta is the weakest (a DOCG name typed only 'region').

ch.title: Switzerland
ch.rationale: Dézaley carries the AOC class (high). La Côte has 'La Côte AOC' as an alias and is also a Vaud sub-region (medium).

at.title: Austria
at.rationale: Labelled 'DAC'; no class to confirm it.

nz-gi.title: New Zealand GIs
nz-gi.rationale: They carry the 'geographical indication' class. A New Zealand GI is the official wine region (assumption, consistent with every label), so they stay regions. Waiheke Island stays under Auckland; North Canterbury's parent 'New Zealand wine' is a country-level item (see that row).

nz-sub.title: New Zealand sub-areas typed 'trademark'
nz-sub.rationale: Gimblett Gravels and Bridge Pa Triangle sit under Hawke's Bay and are typed 'trademark' (a growers' mark, not a GI). Proposed: subregion of Hawke's Bay, so lookup gives subregion plus region Hawke's Bay. Or keep them as regions.

nz-country.title: 'New Zealand wine' (country-level item)
nz-country.rationale: Typed 'aspect in a geographic region': it is New Zealand viticulture, not a wine region. It is North Canterbury's parent, so lookup would offer 'New Zealand wine' as North Canterbury's region.

cl-do.title: Chilean DOs (typed PDO)
cl-do.rationale: Typed 'Protected designation of origin'. In Chile the DO names are the official wine regions, subregions and zones (Valle Central ⊃ Valle del Rapel ⊃ Colchagua/Cachapoal), so they stay regions. Wikidata gives them no parent links.

other-designation.title: Other designation evidence
other-designation.rationale: Don Valley (RU) is typed 'designation of origin'. Nemea (GR, a PDO in reality) carries only an unlabelled class (Q2555824). Register check needed.

other-region.title: Other regions with non-designation extra classes
other-region.rationale: The extra classes are geographic or administrative (settlement, valley, landscape, district, town, region of Western Australia, Hungarian small region). Nothing suggests a designation, so they stay regions. Recaș, Silagiu and Koelenhof are towns typed as wine regions: a data-quality note only.

questions.Q-PT-SUB: Portuguese DOC sub-regions (19, e.g. Borba under Alentejo): model them as appellations with their parent DOC (recommended), or as subregions?
questions.Q-PT-IPR: Portuguese IPRs (9): accept them as appellations now, or wait for an IVV register check of which are still IPRs and which were promoted or merged?
questions.Q-DOURO: Douro/Port: approve RDD as a region with no parent (breaking the RDD↔Port loop), Douro (DOC) and Port Wine as appellations under it, and dropping the 'Região Demarcada do Douro' alias from Douro (DOC)?
questions.Q-MADEIRA: Madeira wine (DOC): keep as the Madeira DOC appellation, or drop it because the item describes the wine?
questions.Q-ARRABIDA: Q2879982 'Arrábida (IPR)' with alias 'Bairrada (DOC)': drop it (recommended until Wikidata is checked), keep it as Arrábida, or treat it as Bairrada DOC?
questions.Q-ES-DUAL: Spanish DOs named like regions (Rioja, Ribera del Duero, Bierzo, Cariñena, Somontano, Pla de Bages, Abona): appellation (recommended) or keep region?
questions.Q-ES-PGI: Spanish PGIs (4): store as appellation (recommended; the slot a label uses), or keep region? Is Ribera del Queiles a PGI (label) or a DO (class)?
questions.Q-IT-DUP: Italian twins (Bivongi, Friuli Annia, Colli Piacentini): keep the DOC-labelled record as the appellation and drop the plain Q14013xxxx twin, or keep both?
questions.Q-NZ-SUB: Gimblett Gravels and Bridge Pa Triangle: subregion of Hawke's Bay, or keep region?
questions.Q-NZ-COUNTRY: 'New Zealand wine' (country-level item): drop it and clear North Canterbury's parent?
questions.Q-CL: Chilean DOs (8): keep as regions (recommended)? Should Rapel ⊂ Valle Central and Colchagua/Cachapoal ⊂ Rapel be added, even though Wikidata has no parent links?
questions.Q-OTHER-REG: Don Valley (RU) and Nemea (GR): accept Don Valley as an appellation on its class alone, and keep Nemea a region until a register check?
questions.Q-MINHO: Minho (VR) / Vinho Verde (DOC): remove the inverted parent link (recommended)? Should Vinho Verde get Minho (VR) as a region parent? (Lookup would then offer 'Minho (VR)' as the region.)
questions.Q-VENTOUX: Côtes du Ventoux AOC: remove its parent link to Côtes du Rhône AOC?
questions.Q-UNESCO: Langhe and Montferrat: remove their parent link to the UNESCO landscape record?
